To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acetylcholine is actively accumulated into synaptic vesicles by a vesamicole-sensitive proton-dependent transporter.
acetylcholine is taken up by synaptic vesicles via a vesamicol sensitive transporter and the uptake is driven by a proton gradient generated via a vacuolar ATPase.
the active uptake of ACh is mediated by the vesamicol-sensitive ACh transporter and that the transporter is coupled to the vesicular H+-ATPase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of acetylcholinesterase activity in synaptic vesicles.
the mechanism of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and the active transport of ACh in synaptic vesicles isolated from brain tissue of the rat.
the molecular mechanism by which the neurotransmitter acetylcholine is taken up by cholinergic nerve terminals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ACh transporter is a proton-driven transporter that is located on the vesicle membrane.
the vesamicol-sensitive acetylcholine transporter is a proton-driven transporter, as is the case for all known vesamicol-sensitive transporters.
the active transport of ACh into the synaptic vesicles is mediated by a proton-dependent transporter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ACh is taken up into the synaptic vesicles by a vesamicoll-sensitive transporter and is released into the synaptic cleft by exocytosis.

ACh transport by synaptic vesicles is mediated by a transporter that is sensitive to vesamicol and 4-ABV, which is dependent on an ATP-dependent proton gradient, and that this transport system is distinct from the vesamicol-sensitive choline transporter.
the active transport of ACh is mediated by a proton symporter that is inhibited by the drugs that are used in vivo to treat Alzheimer's disease and other neurological disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ACh transporter is present in synaptic vesicles and is responsible for the active uptake of ACh.
the vesicular ACh transporters of the brain and the neuromuscular junction are structurally similar.
the vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT) is not a proton antiport.
